text:
Maya: Heads-up — hitting a weird failure on Pixel 3 emulator (API 24). Streaming multipart upload with chunked transfer + our SDK retry policy: first attempt succeeds but a retry sometimes returns 403. Repro locally on emulator only :facepalm:
Ken: Can you paste the logs and which okhttp/retrofit versions?
Maya: okhttp 4.11.0, retrofit 2.9.0. Logs show initial 200, then a server 503 triggers a retry and the second attempt gets 403 with no body. No obvious stacktrace, just server-side deny.
Priya: That smells like a non-repeatable RequestBody. Are you streaming from an InputStream directly?
Maya: Yup, we write FileInputStream in RequestBody#writeTo. Works fine on real devices, fails on emulator / older TLS. My hunch: connection reuse + TLS handshake/close mid-stream -> okhttp retries on a reused socket and server rejects the resumed request.
Sam: OkHttp can do transparent retries for recoverable I/O exceptions, but if the body is non-repeatable the retry will fail in surprising ways. Also interceptor ordering can cause body consumption.
Ken: Quick check — your logging interceptor is after the auth interceptor? If logging reads the body it can drain it early and make it non-repeatable.
Maya: Oh — we had logging before auth (so logging consumed body bytes). I swapped them and tried again.
Priya: Still risky for larger files. A safer pattern: buffer small uploads (<=1MB) so they become repeatable, otherwise disable automatic retries for streaming. Example interceptor ordering and buffering:
```
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(new AuthInterceptor()) // add auth first so it doesn't see an already-consumed body
  .addInterceptor(new HttpLoggingInterceptor().setLevel(HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.BODY))
  .build();

// Simple buffering wrapper for small files
class BufferingRequestBody extends RequestBody {
  private final byte[] buf;
  BufferingRequestBody(InputStream in, long max) {
    // read into memory up to max, throw if larger
  }
  // implement contentType(), contentLength(), writeTo() using buf
}
```
Maya: After swapping interceptors and using a BufferingRequestBody for our ~500KB logs, the emulator retry scenario stopped reproducing.
Ken: Buffering is ok for small artifacts, not for big uploads. SDK change proposal: add a flag `disableRetriesForStreaming` and a heuristic that disables retries when contentLength() == -1.
Sam: Agree. Also add a visible note in onboarding FAQ: "Streaming uploads may not be replayable; prefer buffered wrapper or disable automatic retries."
CI-bot: created PR #2043 to add the config flag + sample to android-samples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/android-sdk/pull/2043
Maya: Tests green on device matrix and emulator. I'll push a short sample to samples/streaming-buffering.md with the wrapper example.
Ken: Filed DX issue DX-489 'non-repeatable body + retry interplay' with repro and workaround. cc @devex for docs follow-up.
Sam: Nice root cause hunt — thanks everyone.
Maya: Leaving a note in onboarding: "If you see 403 after a retry on emulator, check interceptor order and buffering." :+1:
